additional_concerns: The source imposes continuing ultimate responsibility despite outsourcing; it does not supply a complete test for effective retention or supervisory discharge. Practical authority and conduct may be evidence, but are not established necessary or sufficient conditions.

Defective records do not alone establish loss of accountability. Conversely, retaining accountability does not establish proper records, operational soundness or fulfillment of all substantive duties.

The register provisions permit specified parties to maintain the register without displacing the Product Provider's ultimate responsibility. The intermediary issuance provision likewise preserves responsibility within its own conditional scope.

Paragraph 15 concerns requested third-party audit or verification of three specified subjects; paragraph 16 concerns a requested legal opinion supporting the application. Neither establishes an outsourcing safe harbour.
No executable meaning or arrangement-specific facts are supplied. Retrieval success and the unsupported structural check establish neither legal sufficiency nor satisfaction of the requirement.
